Net tone: still modestly positive on growth and labor, but further tempered once viewed through the Financial Stability Report lens. The FSR links softer fundamentals to tighter market liquidity and more fragile valuations, so “soft” business investment and below-target inflation raise vulnerability (Economic Fundamentals influences Market Liquidity/Valuations). Risk appetite looks more cautious: declining 10-year Treasury yields relative to cap rates and reduced investor appetite for corporate bonds point to a risk-off tilt. Elevated attention to credit standards in leveraged loans and greater exposure among near‑prime/subprime borrowers add fragility, even as bank stress tests bolster resilience. Overall, the FSR perspective nudges the stance more cautious than a pure macro read.
